To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of moisture is significant for bulk images, but not for single kernel images.
colour and textural characteristics of bulk grain samples are affected by moisture content, whereas morphological characteristics of single kernel images are not.
the effect of moisture on colour and morphological features was significant for bulk grain images, whereas the effect on texture features was not significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an image processing system to measure the moisture content of grains and the effect of moisture on the physical characteristics and classification capability of grain kernels.
the effect of moisture on grain appearance and kernel morphology, as well as the effect on the classification capability for grain quality.
the development of a machine vision system for grain grading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
moisture content does affect the classification capability of grain images, however the effect of moisture on the classification capability was not significant.
moisture content does have some effect on the physical appearance and the kernel morphology of grains.
the effect of moisture on the classification capability is not as significant as previously reported in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
colour features of bulk grain image are affected more than the textural features by the change in moisture content.
moisture content has a significant effect on the classification capability for colour, morphology and texture features of imaged grain.
the colour and textural properties of the bulk grain images were sensitive to the moisture content and the moisture content of the grains could be determined by using these properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
moisture content has an effect on grain appearance and kernel morphology, which can potentially be exploited to develop a non-destructive method to measure moisture content of grains.
colour features are more effective for moisture classification than the textural and morphological features.
colour and textural feature extraction from bulk grain images are more sensitive to moisture changes than single kernel images.
